terminologyRules: Pneumonia is pulmonary parenchymal inflammation and is not synonymous with cough or upper respiratory disease.
An aspiration event, aspiration pneumonitis and secondary bacterial aspiration pneumonia are separate authored states.
Fever, CBC change or radiographic severity alone never proves bacterial etiology.
Respiratory stabilization and minimal handling precede radiography or airway sampling in an unstable patient.
Oropharyngeal or nasal swabs are not substitutes for a meaningful lower-airway sample.
Blood culture may support selected severe cases but is not presented as an equivalent replacement for lower-airway sampling.
Fungal and parasitic branches require compatible geography, species and exposure.
Clinical, hematologic and imaging recovery may occur at different rates and remain time-linked.
Oxygenation, imaging, culture truth, primary cause and response are authored before player choice and persist through reload.
Drug, dose, duration, oxygen target, sampling, intubation and ventilation technique require separately approved protocols.

familyValidationRules: Reject if oxygen and minimal handling are delayed for radiography or sampling in respiratory distress.

Reject if nonresolving disease only broadens treatment instead of reopening structural, fungal, parasitic and neoplastic mimics.
Reject if the generator creates an antimicrobial, drug, dose, oxygen target, ventilation setting or invasive sampling technique.
